title: Johnian Flight Simulator
intro: St John's College and the Backs, extruded from OpenStreetMap. Fly through the five gold rings over the landmarks. Cambridge City Council has not approved any of this.
address: The Samuel Butler Room, St John's College, CB2 1TP. Postcode for the satnav. You are not a satnav.
noPilot: Your pilot today: an unnamed postgrad on a stipend.
controls: pitch (nose down / up, like a real plane)
start: Click or press Space to take off
paused: Paused. Click or press Space to continue
restart: Click or press Space to fly again

markers.sbr: Samuel Butler Room: the graduate society of St John's since 1960, and its room at I2 First Court with a TV, a Wii, a pool table, a piano and board games.
markers.gsr: Graduate Study Room: 1 All Saints Passage, across St John's Street. Your University Card gets you in. A plane does not.
markers.chapel: St John's College Chapel, by George Gilbert Scott, finished in 1869. Its tower is the tallest thing you are about to hit.
markers.bridge: The Bridge of Sighs, 1831, by Henry Hutchinson. It links Third Court to New Court over the Cam. Do not fly under it. Fine, try.
markers.gate: The Great Gate, early 1500s, with the college arms: two yales holding the shield, the eagle on top. St John's was founded in 1511.

allVisited: All five landmarks done. The Porters' Lodge asks that you land, ideally not on the grass.
offMap: You have left the college. The Porters' Lodge is radioing you back.
landed: Landed. A porter is walking over with a clipboard.
Touchdown. Please do not park on the Backs.
Landed. That will be GBP1.50 on UPay for the parking.

building: You flew into a listed building. The Domestic Bursar has been informed.
Impact! The building was there first, in some cases since the 1500s.
The building wins. It usually does in Cambridge.
ground: You hit the ground too hard. Keep off the grass also applies to aircraft.
Hard landing. The groundsmen will never forgive you.
You found the ground. It was where everyone said it would be.
water: You ditched in the Cam. A punt tour is already selling tickets to the wreck.
Splashdown in the Cam. The ducks have filed a complaint.
You landed on the river. The punt chauffeurs want their commission.

facts: The Samuel Butler Room was founded in 1960 for St John's postgraduates.
Samuel Butler studied at St John's from 1854 to 1858, long before powered flight.
BA Table is on Tuesdays and Fridays in full term. Port & Sherry follows on Fridays, GBP1.50.
The SBR room is in I2, First Court: TV with a Wii, pool table, piano, board games, a small kitchen.
The Graduate Study Room (GSR) is at 1 All Saints Passage.
The Bridge of Sighs was built in 1831 by Henry Hutchinson.
The SBR address: The Samuel Butler Room, St John's College, CB2 1TP.
